Hi Alyssa — thanks for the certificate and context. Looping in Finance (Lauren) and Legal (Priyom) so we can confirm acceptance criteria and next steps. A few clarifying items from our side to speed review: 

1) Billing entity match — The resignation question: is the invoice "bill-to" entity the parent (Partners Holdings LLC) or one of the subsidiaries? Our policy requires that the certificate either list the invoiced legal entity or include a binding affidavit mapping the parent certificate to the specific billing EIN(s).

2) Certificate fields — The scanned image looks signed but the EIN field on the certificate is the parent EIN (you masked it in the email). If you can provide an unredacted copy for internal review (we treat documents as confidential), that will help.

3) State-by-state applicability — For a number of states, resale exemptions do not apply to SaaS/digital services. We’ll run the certificate through our nexus/resale matrix and let you know which states we can accept it for.

4) Preferred documentation — To clear invoice hold quickly we typically accept one of the following:
   - Amended blanket certificate that names the billed legal entity(s) and EIN(s); or
   - A signed mapping affidavit on company letterhead that ties the parent certificate to the billed EINs + a W-9 for the billing entity; or
   - For marketplace sellers, state-specific marketplace carve-out evidence (if applicable).

I’m attaching our internal intake checklist to show exactly what fields we need. If you can send a signed affidavit and a W-9 for the billing entity, that will likely be the fastest route. Priyom — any additional legal red flags here?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Revenue Ops (Redwood Inference)
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
